## Purpose and selected system

Use the existing SimplePad LC examples to ask where a selected mode stores
energy and what loss estimate follows from the stated assumptions. The system
is a pad and surrounding Ground above a substrate, with an explicitly authored
linear inductive/junction treatment. Reuse those notebooks rather than making
an unloaded Eigenmode case appear to be an EPR example.

## Model and analysis choices

Preserve the LC model's conductor ownership, load, stack, vacuum region and
exterior treatment. Specify the requested bulk domains, surface interfaces
and port/junction contributions. Metal–air, metal–substrate and substrate–air
interfaces have distinct ownership and field-side meaning.

Interface thickness, permittivity and loss tangent are explicit assumptions
with provenance. Keep their selected representation separate from the bulk
material model. State the energy denominator and the selected mode/pass before
combining participation or loss quantities. Concrete properties, integration
settings, mesh controls and field retention belong to the notebook.

::: {.callout-note}
Participation, assumption-based loss and native Q are different outputs.
Neither mode frequency nor successful execution supplies missing field energy
or a measured lifetime.
:::

## Workflow

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Palace

Use [SimplePad Palace LC/EPR](../../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/SimplePad/palace_eigenmode.ipynb).
Prepare the selected interface and port treatment, retain mesh/field provenance
through the solve, and resolve the returned energy contributions for the
requested mode. Keep bulk, surface and signed port views identifiable.

### AEDT

Use [SimplePad HFSS LC/EPR](../../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/SimplePad/aedt_hfss_eigenmode.ipynb).
Inspect native interface and junction selections, solve with the requested
saved fields, and evaluate the selected native field integrals. Resolve those
observations with their mode/pass and normalization identity.

:::

## Expected outputs

Retain native selected surfaces/volumes, material and assumption provenance,
saved fields and raw integral evidence. Report energy contributions,
participations and any assumption-based loss estimate with units and
normalization. Native Q, when requested and returned, is labeled separately.

Compare backend results only with their actual representation and boundary
choices visible. This requirement introduces no cross-backend agreement
threshold or loss target.
